notes:
Passed the acceptance gate on the fake backend (backend fake, evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is {kind: model, model_id: deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017, run_id: wP-048} and reviewed_by stays null; no hardware was attached and no hardware backend was run. No deviation from the card: the family-config decision and the MujocoDriver helper express the real interface; the card has no entry_symbols, and the five MJCF model files exist in the clone at the pinned commit. The package serves the card's models[0], playground/open_duck_mini_v2/xmls/scene_rough_terrain_backlash.xml, as a simulated R0 world.sim. cap.world.step.v1 writes the 14 actuator targets and the bridge checks action.ctrl per actuator against the model's actuator_ctrlrange; the 14 position actuators set inheritrange=1, so each interval is the range of the joint it drives. cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults. The rough scene includes open_duck_mini_v2_backlash.xml; the other four card models are not served (the upstream inference script's own default is scene_flat_terrain.xml at playground/open_duck_mini_v2/mujoco_infer.py:257), so changing model_path and the facts serves another scene. MuJoCo was not installed and could not be installed where the gate runs, so the fake backend is this package's stand-in mujoco module (fake.py), passed as the imported class object so the MuJoCo family serves it as the upstream simulator backend; the lock records the schema-required entry-point string .fake:FakeMujoco, as the MuJoCo exemplar does. The stand-in parses the scene and its include for the joint and actuator layout and the inherited control ranges, but integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated joint toward its target, loads no mesh, texture, hfield, contact, equality or tendon data, and was never compared with the real engine. The sim path (a backend not named in backends, which imports the real mujoco) was not run. The stand-in's time step is MuJoCo's library default because the model's option element sets no timestep; it is marked # placeholder in fake.py, and the 2.0 ms in the generated reference is derived from the stand-in, not a Fact or a Limit. Expected warnings: G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because the gate classifies a MuJoCo-family backend as the upstream simulator and does not wrap our stand-in in a recording fake (the bridge-boundary checks still ran), and G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived inputs ticks, action.ctrl and seed (the family derives them; declaring actions would expose undescribed reset fields, as the Gymnasium exemplar notes). No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings: every Fact cites a clone line that exists. There are no operator-required limits, so no site-limits.example.json is needed, and no catalogue request: only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are used, no x-cap id. The card's upstream licence is NOASSERTION with license_class unknown and needs_recon license; the lock records the card's value, and the publication review must resolve the licence. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
